s1.syndrome_frame: exertional dyspnea and palpitations with evidence of right heart strain and possible pulmonary vascular obstruction
salient_findings: dilation of the main pulmonary artery with a hypodense mass
markedly decreased blood flow throughout both lungs
key_facts: 1-month history of exertional dyspnea
1-month history of palpitations
systolic murmur on examination
moderate tricuspid regurgitation on bedside transthoracic ultrasound
possible pulmonary hypertension
dilation of the main pulmonary artery
hypodense mass in the main pulmonary artery with areas of calcification
mass nearly obliterates the lumens of the main and hilar pulmonary arteries
no attachment to the pulmonary valve
no extension into the peripheral branches
markedly decreased blood flow throughout both lungs on lung perfusion scintigraphy
elevated plasma D-dimer level at 1.9 μg/mL

shortlist.label: Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension
shortlist.why_kept: evidence of pulmonary vascular obstruction and elevated D-dimer level

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Artery Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: hypodense mass in the main pulmonary artery with areas of calcification

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Embolism with Saddle Embolus
shortlist.why_kept: systolic murmur, moderate tricuspid regurgitation, and markedly decreased blood flow throughout both lungs

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Artery Thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: dilation of the main pulmonary artery and possible pulmonary hypertension

shortlist.label: Takayasu Arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: possible pulmonary vascular obstruction and systemic symptoms such as exertional dyspnea and palpitations

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of exertional dyspnea, palpitations, and systolic murmur, combined with the imaging findings of a hypodense mass with calcification in the main pulmonary artery, dilation of the main pulmonary artery, and markedly decreased blood flow throughout both lungs, is most consistent with Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension. The elevated D-dimer level also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Artery Sarcoma
rejected.why: While the mass in the pulmonary artery could suggest a tumor, the presence of calcification and the patient's overall clinical presentation are more consistent with a thromboembolic process.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Embolism with Saddle Embolus
rejected.why: The chronic nature of the patient's symptoms and the presence of calcification in the mass suggest a more chronic process than an acute pulmonary embolism.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Artery Thrombosis
rejected.why: This diagnosis is not specific enough to account for the patient's entire clinical presentation, including the exertional dyspnea and palpitations.

rejected.label: Takayasu Arteritis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of inflammation or involvement of other large arteries to support this diagnosis.
